articles.title: Parte médico de Mbappé: hiperextensión de la cápsula posterior de la rodilla izquierda
articles.standfirst: El francés pasó pruebas en Madrid tras lesionarse en el Turquía-Francia
articles.summary: El francés pasó pruebas en Madrid tras lesionarse en el Turquía-Francia
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé sufre una "hiperextensión de la cápsula posterior de la rodilla izquierda". Así lo ha anunciado el Real Madrid en un parte médico tras las pruebas médicas a las que ha sido sometido en la Ciudad Deportiva de Valdebebas. El francés se lesionó en la segunda parte del partido de la Nations League ante Turquía, justo en la jugada en la que metió el único tanto del encuentro. Disparó Mbappé con la derecha y se lesionó en la izquierda. Se encendieron todas las alarmas, en Francia, que le liberó de manera inmediata, y el Madrid, que cruzaba los dedos para tener cuando acabe el parón. Se estima una baja de 10-12 días. La lesión se produce en la rodilla izquierda, la articulación que tanta guerra le dio entre los meses de diciembre y marzo. En este caso, el contratiempo le deja solo como duda para el próximo partido de Liga a la vuelta del parón, el próximo diez de octubre en el Bernabéu ante el Villarreal, aunque por el tiempo de baja tiene bastantes opciones de llegar. No son malas noticias sin duda después de ver los gestos de dolor del delantero tras marcar de nuevo con Francia y escuchar las declaraciones de Zidane en la sala de prensa, en las que aseguró que ya era baja para lo que quedaba de concentración y que la lesión no tenía buena pinta. En el Real Madrid, por su parte, la noticia de la lesión de Mbappé no ha caído bien aunque haya sido al final menos de lo esperado. En el club blanco siguen viendo cómo recuperan a jugadores para dejarlos marchar con sus selecciones y después que vuelvan a Madrid para recuperarse. Ya cayó Konaté ante que Kylian también con Francia. Y ayer mismo el seleccionador de Marruecos, Mohamed Ouahbi, reconocía que Brahim estaba de momento al margen del grupo por unas molestias pero que se quedaba en la concentración para intentar recuperarse para el siguiente partido. De hecho, no jugó en el primer partido ante Gabón (2-0). El Madrid cruza los dedos ahora para lo que queda de parón, que no es poco. De los doce jugadores de Mourinho que se marcharon para los compromisos internacionales, quedan diez. El objetivo es que lleguen todos sanos, sobre todo pensando en la cita ante el Barça en el Camp Nou el próximo 25 de octubre que se antoja crucial de cara a las opciones para el título. Mbappé había jugado hasta ahora prácticamente todo con Mourinho y atravesaba un buen momento como se vio de nuevo con Francia. El parón le sirve ahora para recuperar, pero tendrá que parar y comenzar un plan al margen del grupo en lo que queda de parón, aunque confía en mantener a la vuelta su buen todo del primer tercio de la temporada.

articles.title: Oldham 1-4 Salford
articles.summary: Salford extended their unbeaten run to five league games and are up to seventh after a 4-1 derby win at Oldham.
articles.body:
Salford winger Luke Molyneux scored in the fifth minute when his cross from the right flew into the far corner, eluding everyone.

A poor clearance from goalkeeper Matt Hudson found Kelly N'Mai, who lobbed him from 30 yards in the 19th minute to make it 2-0.

Oldham halved the deficit in the 21st minute when Calum Kavanagh fired home a shot low to the left of keeper Will Norris.

There was a bizarre incident at the end of the opening half when referee Isaac Searle signalled four added minutes but blew his whistle after three. When his attention was drawn to the error, he beckoned the players back on to complete the time.

Salford restored their two-goal advantage in the 57th minute when Brendan Wiredu squeezed a shot past Hudson, and substitute Adebola Oluwo headed home in the 81st minute from Luke Garbutt's free-kick as the Latics fell to a fourth straight league loss.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Scotland: What we learned from Pocognoli's first game
articles.summary: BBC Sport Scotland picks out what we learned from Sebastien Pocognoli's first game in charge as Scotland drew with Slovenia.
articles.body:
New head coach Sebastien Pocognoli said his Scotland bow against Slovenia was "two games in one game" as his side claimed a Nations League point after a much-improved second half showing.

The Scots struggled in a disjointed first half, but took control of the game in the second period and created enough chances to win, but had to settle for a 0-0 draw.

"First half, was not what we expected in terms of structure, " Pocognoli told BBC Scotland.

"We were in between for the press, actually we were a little bit surprised about the formation of Slovenia, but at half-time we fixed this and you can see that the second half was much better.

"We produced what we wanted to show every minute, but first half we learned to stick together, to defend the box, to be resilient and to be patient to change the game."

There were two debuts in Ljubljana, a return for Oli McBurnie, and a change of shape after seven years of Steve Clarke ended after the World Cup in the summer.

It is only the first of four games in this international window, but here are the key takeaways from Pocognoli's debut.

Scotland begin Pocognoli era with encouraging Slovenia draw

'Eternally grateful' McBurnie ready to show what Scotland have missed

Napoli midfielder Billy Gilmour missed the World Cup campaign after a heartbreaking injury against Curacao in Scotland's final home warm-up game.

He returned to the heart of midfield alongside Lewis Ferguson and, according to former Scotland midfielder John Collins was "the catalyst for everything" in the second half.

"Straight from the start of the second half he was getting the ball, playing forward passes and following his pass to the strikers," Collins said.

Gilmour played further up the pitch than Ferguson, "close to a creative 10" according to former Scotland winger Pat Nevin, and played 32 passes into the final third, more than any player on the pitch.

The former Chelsea man combined well with McBurnie on the edge of the box to set up a shot for himself; he slipped in Robbie Ure who opted to cross rather than shoot; and picked out Kieron Bowie with a wonderful through ball which should have resulted in a goal.

Those were just a handful of his key moments. Pocognoli spoke afterwards about the half-time tweak to bring Gilmour deeper to make it harder for Slovenia to play through them and have greater control of the ball.

"We fixed the position of Billy to be a little bit lower and to have Oli McBurnie a little bit more in his box, with two sixes and two 10s, and we were more compact to regain the ball when we lost it.

"Also, that creates some imbalance in the defence from Slovenia, where we can go through the lines with a good chance of Billy or through the depth with the chance of Kieron Bowie or with some crosses.

"He's a fantastic player, I really like him. He's a creative player who always looks forward, always ready to find a solution with a clear game plan, also a good presence around the box and also very good defensively."

Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh was one of two debutants in Slovenia, playing on the left of a back three despite being right footed.

Scotland struggled defensively at times in the first half, with Slovenia playing over the top of them, but Welsh's positioning after the break also helped change the game.

In the first half, his average position was short of the halfway line, but by the end of the game it was in Slovenian territory.

His most common pass went from being to his fellow centre-back Scott McKenna, to Andy Robertson at wing-back.

"It was the starting position of the back three for which changed it - they were in a really good starting position," former Scotland defender Callum Davidson told BBC Scotland.

"In the first half they were quite deep and worried about the ball over the top. But we managed to nullify that and then keep the ball."

The former Motherwell and Celtic defender created a clear goalscoring chance with a wonderful through ball to Bowie, and he finished the game with 16 passes into the final third and the highest accuracy rating.

More aggressive play from Welsh helped set the tone after the break, as he looked assured on his international debut.

With a new manager, injuries to Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland, and on the back of his strong form with Hull City, Oli McBurnie made his first Scotland appearance since 2021 in attack.

Ure, fresh from his move from Sirius in Sweden to Sevilla, made his debut while Sassuolo's Kieron Bowie came off the bench in the second half.

Those three have one club goal between them this season - Bowie's against Juventus - and none for Scotland in their limited caps.

All three were presented chances to score in the second half, though. McBurnie nicked possession and went through, but failed to round Jan Oblak in the Slovenia goal.

His header from a corner was also beaten away by the Atletico Madrid's goalkeeper. Ure drove a low shot off the post in the first half from outside the box, a difficult chance, but then later opted to go for a cut back when slipped in by Gilmour.

Bowie ended with the highest expected goals rating in the Scotland team (0.94) despite playing only 25 minutes - after twice staring at the whites of Oblak's eyes and failing to find the net.

It is only one game, and Scotland will not face a goalkeeper of Oblak's quality in every match, but there is a lingering concern about the national side's goalscoring ability - they have managed one in their last four competitive games.

For all the positives the attackers brought in the second half in general play, do Scotland have someone with a killer instinct?

"International level is all about taking your chances, you don't get too many," Davidson said.

"It's about being really clinical, so for these strikers it's important when you get games like this to take your chances. That's the disappointment from today."

images.caption: Image caption, Scotland defender Stephen Welsh (purple number five) played on the front foot for Scotland

articles.title: Slovenia 0-0 Scotland: What did Sebastien Pocognoli change in first game as Scottish boss since replacing Steve Clarke?
articles.summary: Scotland drew 0-0 with Slovenia in Sebastien Pocognoli's first game in charge; it is the first time Scotland haven't been led by Steve Clarke since 2019; despite failing to win, there were plenty of positives for Pocognoli to take from the game
articles.body:
On the surface, 0-0 against Slovenia doesn't exactly scream entertaining. On another day though, Scotland could've either won by four or lost by a couple; such was the nature of the contest.

In the first half they looked vulnerable, but the second completely dominant. So, what exactly did Pocognoli do to change things up for the better, and what does he still need to keep his eye on?

High press creates chances, but leaves Scots exposed

Despite his record of qualifying for more major tournaments than any other manager, the one criticism Steve Clarke repeatedly received during his tenure was that Scotland sat too deep.

Pre-match, Pocognoli made a point of emphasising that his ideology was the opposite. "I try to be a little bit higher up the pitch," he said.

"On the ball we need to have patterns, which is the most difficult part. But off the ball, we need to be solid. That doesn't mean dropping off though; we need to be higher."

What that created at the start was far more exposure to Angus Gunn's goal. In the first 30 minutes, Slovenia had a goal ruled out and missed numerous other chances. All it would take was one ball over the top of the Scotland backline, and they were in.

Andy Robertson and Stephen Welsh were caught out several times in particular and it was the hosts' poor finishing that kept them from going ahead in that period.

However, when Scotland did finally get to grips with the game, the benefits of the high press came to the fore. It created a glorious chance which Oli McBurnie squandered and helped keep a chaotic tempo which suited Pocognoli's men and kept Slovenia very much on the edge.

It needs some fine-tuning, but with the likes of John McGinn and Scott McTominay when he returns, there's enough energy and quality to make the most of this change in approach.

Pocognoli's formation was similar to what we have seen from Scotland previously. A 3-5-2. However, it was not a defensive set-up.

Aaron Hickey and Andy Robertson had far more license to get forward and the former picked up some lovely areas when entering narrower positions. The wing-backs' main priority was to attack, something that was rarely the case under Clarke. This was further emphasised when Ben Gannon-Doak came on to replace Hickey in the latter stages in search of a breakthrough.

The right and left-sided centre-backs were also a bit more adventurous. On a couple of occasions, Jack Hendry was allowed to roam almost as far up as the Slovenia penalty area to add more numbers.

It was also intriguing to see Stephen Welsh operate on the left of the back three. With the left-footed Scott McKenna central, it would've seemed to have made more sense to swap the two around. However, Welsh's passing was key in trying to split Slovenia open. That was most apparent when he managed to slide in substitute Kieron Bowie, who was thwarted by Jan Oblak.

There was a lot more emphasis on Billy Gilmour to pull the strings in midfield and use his technical ability to open up Slovenia after Scotland won back possession in more dangerous areas. And when the game was stretched, John McGinn was the driving force to get the midfield up the pitch.

The front two both had reasons to prove themselves. In Robbie Ure you had a debutant looking to make his mark and in McBurnie you had a man looking for redemption after five years out of the reckoning.

Neither scored, but both could've. Ure hit the post, while McBurnie made a mess of a glorious one-on-one and saw a thumping header kept out at point-blank range by Jan Oblak.

The way Scotland pressed, you could see someone like a Lyndon Dykes, who wasn't in the squad, having a positive impact. But Pocognoli is ushering in a new era with new players. And his front two certainly posed questions and had a couple of moments of nice interplay.

McBurnie especially is a good option for the midfielders to play and run off. In one moment where Scotland won the ball back high up the pitch, the Hull City man became a wall for Gilmour, creating a good opening. That is where he shone and could continue to be a nuisance in Pocognoli's search for high-pressing breakthroughs.

What the players made of Pocognoli's changes

Scotland striker Oli McBurnie speaking with BBC Sport:

"It took us a little bit of getting used to in the first half, the new formation. I thought once we did, we looked really good. We created enough chances to kill the game. We are really disappointed we didn't get the three points.

"I was asked to play a different position and I quite enjoyed it. I like the manager's ideas; we've had some good chats about it already. It suited me in there, but I won't be able to sleep tonight with those chances. It's a tough one but I'd rather be getting into those positions than not getting the chances.

"We had them pinned for a lot of the game. We put them under waves of pressure. The only thing missing was a goal or two."

Scotland striker Stephen Welsh speaking with BBC Sport:

"We struggled to get into the game in the first half. Obviously it's a new style, some fresh faces and a new way of playing. In the second half, we completely dominated the game. At this level, you need to take your chances. But it's something we can improve on. Definitely positives to come from the game.

"The manager told us at half-time to be a bit sharper on the counter-press. We changed shape at half-time to get more control in the midfield and I thought it worked really well for us.

"I've played on the left-hand side for the last couple of years now. I'm very comfortable doing that. As long as you're in the starting XI, that's the important thing."

November 13 - North Macedonia (H) 7.45pm

articles.title: Entretenidas y justas tablas en Balaídos
articles.standfirst: Celta y Sabadell buscaron la victoria pero con problemas para generar en ataque
articles.summary: Celta y Sabadell buscaron la victoria pero con problemas para generar en ataque
articles.body: Reparto de puntos, tan justo como entretenido, entre Celta Fortuna y Sabadell, dos equipos que quieren hacerse con un hueco en la Segunda división, en el caso de los arlequinados siendo la revelación del campeonato hasta la fecha. Ambos buscaron la victoria pero sin conseguir generar excesivo peligro en las áreas. De este modo, el filial enlaza ya tres jornadas sin ganar, pero al menos vuelve a sumar ante su afición, mientras los arlequinados continúan sin ganar a domicilio tras cuatro salidas. Estuvo mejor en la primera parte el filial céltico, adelantándose en el marcador tras un error de la defensa visitante. Así Álvaro Marín aprovechó una mala cesión de cabeza de Miki Codina hacia su área para recoger el balón y batir con un potente disparo a Fuoli. No tardó en llegar el empate, cuando Édgar González, en un fallo en la marca, cabeceó con potencia un córner muy bien puesto por Ton Ripoll. En el segundo tiempo el Sabadell intentó proponer más y buscar la portería de Coke Carrillo, de hecho Ángel Baena, ingresado en el descanso, marcó el segundo para el cuadro arlequinado, pero estaba en fuera de juego cuando recibió de Urri. A ambos conjuntos les costó generar en ataque, aunque Édgar le ganó el duelo aéreo a Álvaro Marín que se disponía a firmar su doblete. Y en el añadido tuvo Ángel Arcos una clara opción que despejó Eneko a córner. El Celta Fortuna deja escapar dos nuevos puntos de Balaídos y se mantiene fuera de la zona roja de la tabla, mientras que el Sabadell sigue apuntando a la zona noble.

articles.title: El Cádiz reacciona, pero sigue sin ganar
articles.standfirst: Vladys igualó en la segunda parte el tanto inicial de Enric Gallego, que ya es el Pichichi en solitario de LaLiga Hypermotion
articles.summary: Vladys igualó en la segunda parte el tanto inicial de Enric Gallego, que ya es el Pichichi en solitario de LaLiga Hypermotion
articles.body: Tenerife y Cádiz no encontraron la manera de pasar del empate en un partido áspero, en el que los amarillos rescataron un empate gracias a su mayor insistencia y al plan fallido de los locales de fiar todo a un contragolpe que terminase de desnivelar la balanza cuando disfrutaban de un exiguo 1-0. Las tablas dejan a los isleños en mitad de la tabla, y sin disipar las dudas que dejó la goleada en Castellón, y a los amarillos antepenúltimos y sin conocer el triunfo en el presente curso. Enric Gallego adelantó al Tenerife en el primer acto para vencer la resistencia de un Cádiz que parece mejor sobre el césped del lugar que ocupa en la clasificación. El equipo de Celades tiene una notable nómina de trescuartistas capaces de generar fútbol en la finca rival con Borja Vázquez, Ibon Sánchez o Antoñito Cordero, pero se desangra en las áreas. En la propia porque los locales rentabilizaron la única opción clara que tuvieron, un balón suelto que cazó Gallego con tanto instinto como habilidad, y en la ajena porque Vladys tardó 74 minutos en llevar a la red una de las numerosas oportunidades de las que dispuso para posibilitar que los andaluces ganasen por vez primera en esta Liga. Los isleños confiaron en que el 2-0 llegase antes que el 1-1, pero la moneda salió cruz esta vez. Sobre todo, porque los suplentes sólo empeoraron aún más el panorama y porque el equipo de Celades nunca bajó los brazos. Gomis, en el alargue, tuvo en sus botas el triunfo del Tenerife, pero su remate raso y rodeado de adversarios se marchó junto al poste izquierdo de David Gil.

articles.title: Eric se lesiona en el calentamiento y juega Pubill
articles.standfirst: El defensa del Barcelona se tuvo que retirar del entrenamiento al sentir molestias en la rodilla izquierda
articles.summary: El defensa del Barcelona se tuvo que retirar del entrenamiento al sentir molestias en la rodilla izquierda
articles.body: El partido entre Inglaterra y España arranca con sobresalto para la selección española. Luis de la Fuente ha tenido que mover el once al lesionarse en el calentamiento Eric García. Su puesto lo ocupa Marc Pubill. Eric notó molestias en la rodilla izquierda, lo que hizo que se retirase del césped en busca del vestuario. Rápidamente se activo a Pubill para que dejase en rondo de los suplentes y pasara a realizae el calentamiento de los titulares. España se queda con un solo lateral derecho en la lista. Iván Fresneda está en la grada al ser uno de los tres descartes de Luis de la Fuente de la lista de 26. La reglamentación de la competición impide que pueda recurrirse a un jugador descartado en caso de lesión entre los 23 elegidos. En el banquillom queda la vía de Zubimendi, que la pasada jornada ocupó esa posición en el Arsenal. Con tres partidos aún por delante, De la Fuente tendrá esperar. El primer analisis habla sólo de moestias y de la elección de no arriesgar. Pero si no mejora de manera clara Eric, habráque llamar a un nuevo jugador. Puede elegir un lateral puro o recurrir a un central y que Pubill y Fresneda se queden como dueños del carril diestro.

articles.title: Vivian, casi a punto
articles.standfirst: ​El pasado lunes ya entrenó junto al grupo una vez superada la pubalgia y todo apunta a que estará disponible para el regreso de la competición ante el Rayo Vallecano
articles.summary: El pasado lunes ya entrenó junto al grupo una vez superada la pubalgia y todo apunta a que estará disponible para el regreso de la competición ante el Rayo Vallecano
articles.body: El largo parón de selecciones entre septiembre y octubre puede ser beneficioso para la enfermería rojiblanca. El central Dani Vivian, ausente tanto en pretemporada como en los primeros compromisos ligueros, afronta la cuenta atrás para volver al verde después de más de dos meses en el dique seco. El campeón de Europa en 2024 no vivió su mejor campaña el pasado año y su rendimiento disminuyó respecto a un curso anterior en el que fue el líder indiscutible de la zaga rojiblanca. Con Edin Terzic incidiendo en hacer de la solidez defensiva uno de los pilares del equipo, Vivian está llamado a ser una pieza clave y su regreso se encuentra en la recta final. El pasado lunes ya entrenó junto al grupo una vez superada la pubalgia y todo apunta a que, para el regreso de la competición ante el Rayo Vallecano, el vitoriano estará disponible. Además, el técnico tendrá una oportunidad previa para probarle en la Euskal Herria Txapela que disputarán los rojiblancos el próximo viernes día 2 ante la Real Sociedad.

articles.title: Finlandia le hace un 'siete' a San Marino con 'hat-trick' de Pohjanpalo
articles.standfirst: El '9' del Palermo se convierte en el cuarto máximo goleador histórico de los 'búhos reales'
articles.summary: El '9' del Palermo se convierte en el cuarto máximo goleador histórico de los 'búhos reales'
articles.body: Joel Pohjanpalo siempre ha sido un goleador de rachas. De marcar goles de dos en dos, de tres en tres... y luego atravesar largas sequías anotadoras. Una 'etiqueta' que volvió a reivindicar en la goleada sobre San Marino (0-7) en el estreno de Finlandia en la UEFA Nations League. El atacante del Palermo, de 32 años, firmó un 'hat-trick' y acumula ya 22 dianas en 90 internacionalidades. Sólo Mikael Forsell (29), Jari Litmanen (32) y Teemu Pukki (43) han marcado más. El propio Pohjanpalo abrió la lata en el 5' al cazar un balón muerto en el área. Ampliaron distancias Adrian Svanback en el 14' -cabeceó un centro de Leo Walta- y Benjamin Kallman, en el 33', llegando desde atrás. Tras el descanso, apareció Leo Walta. El mediapunta de Los Angeles FC se lució con dos golazos, a cada cual mejor. Primero, en el 50', sorprendió a Edoardo Colombo con un derechazo a la escuadra desde la frontal. En el 55', con San Marino jugando con 10 por la expulsión de Alessandro Golinucci en el 51', resolvió con un tiro al palo largo tras un gran eslalon. Hubo tiempo para que Pohjanpalo rematara su 'hat-trick' con dos nuevos goles. En el 79' resolvió con el exterior un mano a mano tras un buen pase filtrado por Svanback y en el 87' convirtió un penalti cometido por Marcello Mularoni sobre Robin Lod.

articles.title: Chris Ramos recupera el '9' para el derbi asturiano
articles.standfirst: El delantero apunta a regresar al once del Oviedo ante el Sporting tras superar sus problemas físicos y con el recuerdo de haber marcado ya a los rojiblancos
articles.summary: El delantero apunta a regresar al once del Oviedo ante el Sporting tras superar sus problemas físicos y con el recuerdo de haber marcado ya a los rojiblancos
articles.body: El derbi asturiano aparece en un momento importante para Chris Ramos. El delantero gaditano comenzó la temporada como la referencia ofensiva elegida por Julián Calero y fue titular en las dos primeras jornadas, ante Granada y Leganés. Precisamente aquel segundo encuentro frenó su continuidad. Chris quedó tocado después de la dura salida de Raúl Fernández en un mano a mano, acción que terminó con la expulsión del guardameta, y posteriormente sufrió también un golpe en la espalda durante una caída. Los problemas físicos terminaron apartándole de los compromisos ante Albacete, Burgos y Valladolid. Su regreso se produjo el pasado fin de semana en Sabadell. Calero recurrió a él al descanso y Chris disputó completa la segunda mitad, sus primeros minutos después de varias semanas sin competir. Una prueba importante antes de un derbi al que llega ya recuperado y con muchas opciones de regresar directamente al once. Las bajas de Carlos Fernández e Isfan han reducido las alternativas del técnico para la punta del ataque y todo apunta a que Chris volverá a ocupar el puesto que ya era suyo al comienzo del campeonato. El delantero suma hasta el momento 214 minutos repartidos en tres encuentros, dos de ellos como titular, y todavía busca su primer gol oficial con la camiseta del Real Oviedo. El domingo tendrá un escenario inmejorable para estrenarse y, además, ante un rival del que guarda un buen recuerdo. Chris Ramos ya sabe lo que es marcarle al Sporting: lo hizo el 25 de abril de 2025, cuando defendía la camiseta del Cádiz, anotando en el minuto 19 el único tanto de la victoria gaditana por 1-0. Ahora, casi año y medio después, volverá a encontrarse con los rojiblancos en un contexto completamente diferente. Chris Ramos tiene ante sí la posibilidad de recuperar la titularidad, estrenarse como goleador azul y hacerlo en el partido más especial del calendario para el Oviedo. Una oportunidad que llega después de que los problemas físicos interrumpiesen un inicio de temporada en el que Calero ya había depositado en él su confianza.

articles.title: Quién es James Trafford, el portero de Inglaterra que juega contra España en la Nations League: el tercer guardameta más caro de la historia
articles.standfirst: Tuchel dejó en el banquillo a Pickford y se decantó por el cancerbero del Leeds
articles.summary: Tuchel dejó en el banquillo a Pickford y se decantó por el cancerbero del Leeds
articles.body: Thomas Tuchel ha sorprendido a todos alineando a James Trafford como portero titular ante España. Jordan Pickford llevaba varios torneos siendo indiscutible en la portería de Inglaterra, como en el pasado Mundial, jugando todos los partidos salvo el tercer y cuarto puesto, en el que jugó Henderson, ahora lesionado. Trafford también fue convocado en la cita de Estados Unidos pero no disputó ni un minuto. Ahora, el portero del Leeds será el encargado de defender la portería británica en Wembley. Este verano, el guardameta fue noticia por su sonado fichaje. Cambió el Manchester City por el Leeds a cambio de 52 millones de euros, convirtiéndose en el cancerbero británico más caro de la historia y en el tercero de la historia, sólo por detrás de Kepa Arrizabalaga (68 millones) y Alisson Becker (62 millones). Trafford, que se quedó sin el puesto de primero portero en el City la temporada pasada ante la llegada de Gianluigi Donnarumma, llega al Leeds tras jugar 17 partidos el curso anterior, la mayoría de ellos en las Copas, y después de no jugar ni un minuto en el Mundial con Inglaterra.

articles.title: Virginia Tech pulls off 21-14 win over Boston College in the middle of nor'easter storm
articles.summary: Hokies head coach James Franklin dubbed the game the 'Tsunami Bowl' ahead of the blustery matchup.
articles.body:
In a win over Boston College on Saturday, Virginia Tech not only had to compete against the Eagles — the Hokies had to fight against Mother Nature.

A nor'easter storm hitting the northeastern United States this weekend put Saturday's game in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts, in the middle of the windy, rainy environment. Heavy rains and wind gusts up to 40 miles per hour gave the game a bit of a challenge, but the Hokies were able to pull to a 21-14 win after a fourth-quarter surge.

Prior to the game, Virginia Tech head coach James Franklin said on ACC Network that the team was preparing for what he called the "Tsunami Bowl."

"When we left Blacksburg, it was like one of the most beautiful fall weekends you've ever seen in your life," Franklin said. "The reality is, both teams have to play under the same conditions, so we're just excited for the opportunity to play the game we love."

Those harsh conditions made for a pretty boring football game at first: Virginia Tech scored the only points of the first half with a field goal as time expired. On a 45-yard attempt, Hokies kicker John Love managed to get the ball between the uprights despite whipping wind and rain that coated the camera lens.

Love added another field goal in the third quarter; by that point, the camera view was even blurrier with rain.

On the next play, though, Boston College made the game more exciting with a go-ahead touchdown, with quarterback Mason McKenzie keeping the ball on a run into the end zone. In the fourth quarter, another McKenzie rushing TD brought the Eagles' lead to 14-6, but Ethan Grunkemeyer 's 14-yard touchdown pass to Marlion Jackson , and the Hokies' successful 2-point conversion, brought the score even.

Virginia Tech then pulled ahead on their next drive, with Jeffrey Overton Jr. breaking loose for a 76-yard touchdown run. That ended up being enough to get the win.

The weather not only impacted the play-calling, the wind and rain left a very small number of people in the stands, with just a few fans braving the elements for the matchup.

For those few BC fans in attendance, it wasn't exactly the ending that the Eagles were hoping for, especially after sitting through the storm. But for Franklin, the Hokies held on to win the Tsunami Bowl and move to 4-0 to start the season.

articles.title: Arch Manning Underwhelms, Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock from Texas' Win vs. Tennessee
articles.summary: Texas earned its fourth win to open the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
Texas earned its fourth win to open the 2026 college football season.

The top-ranked Longhorns went on the road and held on to beat No. 14 Tennessee 20-17 in Knoxville.

They struggled to get much breathing room until a four-yard touchdown run from Raleek Brown in the fourth quarter made it a two-score game inside the final six minutes.

The Vols nearly pulled off the improbable as true freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon hit Mike Matthews for a 30-yard touchdown pass with 1:22 remaining. Tennessee then recovered the ensuing onside kick.

The offense went backward and couldn't get into field-goal range. Brandon's Hail Mary attempt as time expired was batted away.

Much like in the comeback victory over Ohio State, Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning didn't have a prolific showing. The result should help his 2027 NFL draft stock on its own, though.

The senior also had moments like this throw to Jermaine Bishop Jr. where the proof of concept was blindingly obvious:

For a quarterback with Manning's reputation, you'd still like to see him put the offense on his back in a way he hasn't much in a big game.

Texas couldn't get much going on the ground. Brown ran for 67 yards and averaged just 3.9 yards per carry.

That didn't make Manning's life easier, but there are always going to be days when a quarterback has little support from the backfield. That's when the QB needs to step up, and Manning didn't do that against Tennessee.

ESPN's Jordan Reid reported at least 10 NFL teams had representatives at Neyland Stadium. Manning wasn't the Texas player who will have impressed them the most.

Longhorns edge-rusher Colin Simmons, the No. 3 overall prospect on Bleacher Report's 2027 big board , had five sacks to tie a single-game record for the program.

Granted, Simmons will need to be wiser with his on-field celebrations.

Texas has a week off before it renews its longstanding rivalry with Oklahoma on Oct. 10 at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas.

The Sooners could be sitting at 2-2 by the time Saturday ends. They play No. 2 Georgia on the road. As unimpressive as their offense has looked, however, their defense was allowing just 215.3 yards per game entering Week 4.

This figures to be another stiff test for Manning and a Texas offense that needs to find better balance.

articles.title: No. 16 Louisville falls to unranked Wake Forest for second loss of the season as 57-yard kick is blocked
articles.summary: Louisville falls to 2-2 and 1-1 in ACC play, putting their chances of an eventual CFP playoff berth in question.
articles.body:
The No. 16 Louisville Cardinals suffered their second loss of the season on Saturday, this one to unranked Wake Forest.

The Demon Deacons clinched a 30-27 upset victory by blocking the Cardinals' 57-yard field-goal attempt which would have sent the game into overtime.

Wake Forest had been on top throughout most of the game. The Demon Deacons took a 24-21 lead into halftime and then kept the Cardinals to just six second-half points to pull off the win.

Louisville entered the game with a 2-1 record. The Cardinals lost their season opener to Ole Miss, but answered back with a blowout win over Villanova and then a conference win over then-No. 16 SMU.

The loss to Wake Forest is Louisville's first ACC loss. The Cardinals still have upcoming games against Florida State, Georgia Tech and North Carolina. Louisville still has a path to the College Football Playoff , but the program's margin for error was significantly reduced by Saturday's loss to Wake Forest.

The Demon Deacons pick up what could become a huge tiebreaker come the end of November. There are plenty of ACC games to get through over the next two months, but as of this game's finish, Louisville is 8th, and Wake Forest is 7th in the conference standings.

The Cardinals struggled to pick up first downs. While Louisville had 24 in the game, the Cardinals had 14 third-down attempts and converted only seven. Louisville went for it on fourth down once and was unsuccessful.

Before the blocked kick, Louisville had been moving the ball well, picking up 39 yards in five plays.

On first-and-10 from the Wake 30, Louisville was called for holding. After losing 10 yards, Cardinals quarterback Lincoln Kienholz had three consecutive incompletions as the pass rush got to him, and he took two especially hard hits.

Unable to pick up any more yards, Louisville had to either go for the Hail Mary and the win, or the 57-yard kick and the tie for overtime.

It was a fairly even game in the box score. Wake Forest had 402 total yards, compared to Louisville's 399. Each team had only one turnover, and there was only a five-yard difference in penalties. The Cardinals even had 33:34 of possession, while the Demon Deacons had 26:26.

The game really came down to the final play, and Wake Forest came up big when it needed it most.

Louisville will go on the road next week to take on NC State. The Demon Deacons will be at home and host Stanford.

articles.title: Doble toque de Kane en el penalti... y libre indirecto para España
articles.standfirst: El inglés mandó al larguero un penalti el que cometió la infracción del doble toque
articles.summary: El inglés mandó al larguero un penalti el que cometió la infracción del doble toque
articles.body: Penalti para Inglaterra. Minuto 54. Lanza Harry Kane. Se resbala, balón al larguero... y la repetición demuestra que hay doble toque. Imposible no acordarse de la acción de Julián Álvarez en la eliminatoria de Champions ante el Madrid. Entonces, el argentino lo marcó y Marciniak lo anuló. En esta ocasión, y tras el cambio de interpretación de la norma, al fallarse la pena máxima, el doble toque se sancionó con libre indirecto para España desde el punto de penalti. Si Harry Kane hubiera marcado, el colegiado del encuentro habría mandado repetir la pena máxima, pues se trata de una infracción involuntaria. En este caso, al fallar, la acción se resuelve con un libre indirecto para la selección. Kane y Bellingham tenían claro quién era el culpable de la situación: el césped. El resbalón del inglés vino propiciado por el estado del terreno de juego en esa zona, algo blando. Mientras, los jugadores de la selección celebraban el fallo de la pena máxima, que había llegado con polémica. Porque cayó Bellingham ante Rodri y Massa no pitó nada. Fue el VAR el que llamó al colegiado para que este rectificara, en una jugada que sigue dejando muchas dudas.

articles.title: Texas Tech LB Austin Romaine gets back-to-back pick 6s in blowout win vs. Sam Houston
articles.summary: Two plays, two pick-sixes for the senior transfer linebacker, who had only tallied one interception in his previous three college football seasons.
articles.body:
No. 11 Texas Tech ran out to a 21-0 lead in an eventual 49-13 win over Sam Houston early in the second quarter. Amazingly, two of those touchdowns came from the defense. And one player scored those TDs, each of them on a pick 6.

On Sam Houston's fourth possession of the game, Red Raiders linebacker Austin Romaine intercepted quarterback Brett Holloway on second-and-10 from the Bearkats ' 19-yard line. The senior LB ran it in 15 yards for the score.

Romaine, a senior transfer from Kansas State, only had one interception in his previous three seasons of college football, getting that last year. The Hillsboro, Missouri, native came into Saturday's game with 119 total tackles, 3.5 sacks, 18.5 tackles for loss and 3 forced fumbles.

Landyn Locke took over at QB on Sam Houston's next possession. But on his very first play, he was picked off by Romaine, who ran the interception back 31 yards for his second pick 6 in two plays.

Sam Houston managed to keep the ball away from Romaine on its next two possessions. The Bearkats punted after six plays on their next series. Then Locke hit passes of 32 yards to Kyan Berry-Johnson and a 52-yarder to Tim Burns Jr. for the score. The Bearkats scored despite 25 yards in penalties during the drive.

Texas Tech QB Will Hammond threw interceptions on the team's next two possessions. The second one came after Sam Houston punter Cal Joseph pinned the Red Raiders at their own 1-yard line. Two plays later, Locke hit Chris Reed for a 9-yard score and cut Texas Tech's lead to 21-14 before halftime.

However, the second half belonged to the Red Raiders, who put four more touchdowns on the board. Hammond got two of them with a 21-yard pass and 23-yard run. The other scores came on a 13-yard rush by Cameron Dickey and a 27-yard pass from backup QB Thomas Castellanos.

Hammond finished with 224 yards on 17-of-29 passing with 1 TD and 3 interceptions. Dickey rushed for 91 yards and 2 scores on 12 carries. And along with his two pick-sixes, Romaine led all defensive players with 8 tackles.

With the win, Texas Tech improved to 4-0, including a win over No. 22 Houston . Up next for the Red Raiders is a visit to Colorado (2-2) before a bye week.

articles.title: De la Fuente 'cambia' la cara de España
articles.standfirst: Baena y Oyarzabal, que entraron en el minuto 55, anotaron los tantos de la remontada.
articles.summary: Baena y Oyarzabal, que entraron en el minuto 55, anotaron los tantos de la remontada.
articles.body: ¿Quién se atreve a cuestionar una decisión de Luis de la Fuente? A España, que se fue al descanso perdiendo 2-1, le tocaba remontar. En los primeros 45 minutos encajó más goles que en todo el Mundial, así que en la segunda parte tocaba ponerse el mono de trabajo. Apenas habían pasado 10 minutos del segundo acto cuando el seleccionador tomó su primera decisión. Decidió retirar a Ferran y Nico, dos de las novedades del once respecto a la final de Nueva York, y apostar por Oyarzabal y Baena, dos indiscutibles durante el torneo en el que nos coronamos con la segunda estrella. Y no falló. Baena, que parece otro cuando se viste con la camiseta de España, tuvo la puntería que le faltó a Ferran y Lamine para, en su primera oportunidad, anotar el empate. Sólo llevaba cinco minutos en el campo, pero el de Roquetas de Mar ajustó un derechazo donde Trafford no podía llegar. Fue su cuarto gol con España. Pero el trabajo de Baena no había terminado. Casi nadie celebró su gol y todos se colocaron para sacar rápido y seguir jugando. Esta selección tiene hambre y un empate no saciaba ese apetito. Por eso fue el propio Baena el que a un cuarto de hora del final vio a Oyarzabal encarar la portería y le regaló una asistencia que lo dejó solo ante Trafford. Esa historia solo entendía un final: gol. Qué manera de definir de Mikel. Cero nervios, cero presión. Un delantero de hielo que tiene su contador de goles ardiendo. Son ya 31 con la selección. Nuestro nueve. Las dos estrellas que España luce en el pecho se reencarnaron durante un rato en Mikel y Alex. Los cambios de De la Fuente que mutaron los errores en aciertos, que convirtieron los "uy" en "gol" y que demostraron porque fueron indiscutibles durante toda la copa del mundo.

images.caption: Oyarzabal celebra el 3-2. CHEMA REY

articles.title: Nations League: Who made an uncharacteristic error? England player ratings v Spain
articles.summary: England were beaten 3-2 in an entertaining game by world champions Spain in the Nations League - here's how BBC Sport rated the Three Lions' players.
articles.body:
England were beaten 3-2 in an entertaining game by world champions Spain in the Nations League - the Three Lions' first match since this summer's World Cup.

Lamine Yamal gave Spain the lead before goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane put England ahead.

Kane then missed a penalty before Alex Baena curled in to level the score, with Mikel Oyarzabal scoring the winner.

Here's how we rated England's players - and you can have your say in the comments at the bottom.

James Trafford: Showed early on his ability to play with the ball at his feet but conceded after just two minutes when Guehi gifted the ball to Lamine Yamal. An important save stopped Torres making it 2-0 in the first half. 6

Jarell Quansah: Continued at right-back after showing what he could do in the position at the World Cup. A physically dominant performance and had a chance to score but headed over. 6

Ezri Konsa: Some shaky moments for Konsa and England's back four but the centre-back regrouped and got better as the game went on. 6

Marc Guehi: An uncharacteristic error gifted the ball - and the opening goal - to Lamine Yamal. 5

Nico O'Reilly: Put in the cross for Kane's goal as England took the lead in the first half. Did a good job of trying to deal with Lamine Yamal. However he gave the ball away for Spain's second goal. 6

Elliot Anderson: Nearly punished for giving the ball away in a dangerous position in the first half but Ferran Torres rolled his shot wide. Anderson and midfield partner Lewis-Skelly took some time to settle in what was a tough night in the middle of the pitch against a Spain side who moved the ball so well. 6

Myles Lewis-Skelly: A first England start in centre midfield for Lewis-Skelly after shining for Arsenal. Given the tough task of trying to shut off the supply to Spain's conductor, Rodri. A solid performance. Replaced after 70 minutes. 6

Jude Bellingham: The Real Madrid midfielder produced another dominant display and was unlucky to be on the losing side. He provided an assist for England's equaliser and won a penalty which Kane hit against the bar after slipping. Stung Simon's palms with a drive in stoppage time. 8

Bukayo Saka: Won a couple of free-kicks around the box and shot over from the edge of the area in the first half. Curled just wide with the score level but a quiet night for the winger. 6

Anthony Gordon: The Barcelona winger scored an excellent goal on the counter-attack. He kept calm when played through on goal by Bellingham when his pace put him clear. A dangerous cross in the first half after England went behind and a threat in behind all night. 8

Harry Kane: Started dropping deep in the first half in search of the ball after England went behind. Scored the second with a deflected header to put England in the lead but missed a penalty when they had the chance to add a third in the second half. 7

James Garner (on 70, Lewis-Skelly): Took on Lewis-Skelly's role of trying to keep Rodri quiet. 6

Morgan Rogers (on 70, Gordon): Did not get much of the ball in his 20 minutes on the pitch. 6

Morgan Gibbs-White (on 83, Saka): Came on and played on the left wing. 6

Calvert-Lewin (on 83, Kane): Not much time to impact the play. 6

Jarrad Branthwaite, (on 89, Guehi): A late change for Guehi in the England backline. No time to make an impression. 6

Subs not used: Pickford, Steele, Alexander-Arnold, Scott, Chalobah, Hall, Eze.

articles.title: Así queda el grupo de España tras la victoria contra Inglaterra en la Nations League
articles.standfirst: La selección española consigue los tres primeros grupos de esta edición
articles.summary: La selección española consigue los tres primeros grupos de esta edición
articles.body: España está asignado en el grupo A3 con Inglaterra, Croacia y República Checa. El objetivo será meterse por tercera vez en una Final Four y lograr su segundo campeonato. Los de Luis de la Fuente han defendido su estatus de campeón sufriendo más que en todo el Mundial. Se pusieron por delante en el marcador en apenas dos minutos con un gol de Lamine pero los ingleses remontaron con tantos de Gordon y Kane. El punto de inflexión se produjo cuando el delantero del Bayern de Múnich falló un penalti, en el que además dio doble toque. Ese error le dio vida a España que notó los cambios de Oyarzabal y Baena, que fueron los goleadores. Con este resultado, la selección española se pone con tres puntos en el grupo. En el otro partido del grupo, Croacia se impuso a la República Checa de Santi Denia por 1-2. En un duelo en el que Modric marcó, para colocar a los croatas primeros, empatados a puntos con España. En el próximo duelo España y Croacia, se disputará el próximo martes 29 de septiembre a las 20:45 horas.

articles.summary: La selección española jugará en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán
articles.body: La Selección Española de fútbol continúa su camino en la UEFA Nations League con su esperado segundo compromiso de la fase de grupos. Tras el debut frente a Inglaterra en Londres con victoria por 2-3, el combinado nacional regresa a territorio nacional para enfrentarse a la combativa selección de Croacia en un duelo crucial por el liderato del Grupo A3 de la Liga A. El encuentro se disputará el próximo martes 29 de septiembre a las 20:45 horas. Este horario unificado fijado por la UEFA para los compromisos de la competición garantiza una velada de máxima expectación futbolística. El escenario elegido para albergar esta cita de nivel internacional es el Estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, ubicado en la ciudad de Sevilla. La capital andaluza volverá a convertirse en el feudo de La Roja, que se ha acostumbrado a ver partido allí en La Cartuja. El España - Croacia de la segunda jornada de la Nations League se disputará a las 20:45 horas. Todos los aficionados podrán seguir el desarrollo del choque en directo y en abierto a través de La 1 de Televisión Española, así como en streaming a través de la plataforma digital RTVE Play.

articles.title: Colin Simmons, Raleek Brown lead No. 1 Texas to SEC-opening road win over No. 14 Tennessee
articles.summary: The Tennessee triumph sends Texas (4-0, 1-0) into its bye on a high note. The Longhorns are off until their annual rivalry game against Oklahoma in Dallas on...
articles.body:
KNOXVILLE, Tenn. - At least this Saturday, " the real UT " was Texas.

Colin Simmons entered the Texas football record books with a five-sack performance, and Raleek Brown scored twice as the No. 1-ranked Longhorns earned a 20-17 win over No. 14 Tennessee at Neyland Stadium. The three-point victory was recorded in the Longhorns' SEC opener.

The Volunteers made things interesting after a touchdown with 1 minute, 22 seconds remaining in regulation cut the Texas lead to three. Tennessee then covered an on-side kick. But a last-second Hail Mary was knocked away by Texas defensive back Jelani McDonald in the end zone.

The Tennessee triumph also sends Texas (4-0, 1-0) into its bye on a high note. The Longhorns are off until their annual rivalry game Oct. 10 against Oklahoma in Dallas. Tennessee (3-1, 0-1) will host Auburn next week.

Texas gets off to a quick start... and then stalls

Texas opened the game with the football, and the Longhorns used seven plays to march down the field. Manning converted 5-, 8- and 43-yard passes along the way before Raleek Brown ended the drive with a 9-yard touchdown run.

Good starts on the road against a ranked opponent had been something that had eluded Texas in recent years. Over the previous three seasons, the Longhorns had been hosted by six ranked opponents. On their first drives in those six games, UT was held to one field goal while averaging 8.3 plays and 31.7 yards per game-opening possession.

Sept. 9, 2023 at No. 3 Alabama : 7 plays, 27 yards (punt)

Sept. 7, 2024 at No. 10 Michigan : 13 plays, 51 yards (missed field goal)

Oct. 26, 2024 at No. 25 Vanderbilt: 5 plays, 17 yards (interception)

Nov. 30, 2024 at No. 20 Texas A&M: 3 plays, 3 yards (punt)

Aug. 30, 2025 at No. 3 Ohio State: 9 plays, 33 yards (turnover on downs)

Nov. 15, 2025 at No. 5 Georgia: 13 plays, 59 yards (field goal)

Texas did not return to the end zone in the first half. The Longhorns eventually took a 10-3 lead into halftime after Tennessee's Cooper Ranvier and Texas' Gianni Spetic exchanged field goals.

Texas compiled 147 yards over 27 first-half plays. Manning threw an interception at Tennessee's 4-yard line during a first half that featured a strange unsportsmanlike conduct penalty that was called after Simmons simulated himself urinating after a sack .

As Colin Simmons makes history, Texas shuts down Tennessee

The Texas offense continued to struggle after the halftime break and went three-and-out on its first offensive possession of the second half. A sack of Manning brought punter Mac Chiumento onto the field, and his 48-yard punt was returned by Tennessee's Qua Moss for a game-tying touchdown. That 57-yard highlight accounted for the first touchdown scored on a punt return against Texas since Jeff Scott did so for Ole Miss in 2013.

Texas quickly regained the lead when Spetic kicked a 44-yard field goal with 9 minutes left in the third quarter. Brown then secured the victory on a 4-yard touchdown run with 5:41 left.

Defensively, Texas dominated a Tennessee that had scored 143 points in its first three games against Furman, Georgia Tech and Kennesaw State. The Volunteers were limited to 151 passing yards and 70 rushing yards.

The Texas pass rush recorded 10 sacks and harassed Tennessee quarterback Faizon Brandon all afternoon. Five of those sacks belonged to Simmons, who tied a school record that Shane Dronett set in 1990 at Texas Tech.

Texas Longhorns defensive end Colin Simmons (1) sacks Tennessee Volunteers quarterback Faizon Brandon (11) in the second quarter of Texas' game against the Tennessee Volunteers at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tennessee, Sept. 26, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman)

articles.title: Marc Cucurella endures night to forget as Spain beat England
articles.summary: Spain came from behind to beat England 3-2
articles.body:
Reigning world champions Spain donned their second star on their jersey for the first time as they took on World Cup semi-finalists England at Wembley Stadium in the UEFA Nations League, securing a 3-2 win to start the campaign.

Real Madrid 's Marc Cucurella played the full 90 minutes but had a tough time up against Arsenal 's Bukayo Saka , as well as being involved in both England goals and having penalty shouts against him.

Lamine Yamal gave Spain an early lead on only two minutes, but Cucurella was caught out as Anthony Gordon played a one-two on the counter attack with Jude Bellingham .

Minutes later, Harry Kane gave England the lead with a header which Cucurella could only knee into his own net. Kane's effort was headed on target, so he avoided an own goal, but he perhaps could have cleared the shot.

Cucurella then had two penalty shouts against him, one for handball and another for bringing down Saka, but Italian referee Davide Massa ignored both. Harry Kane did miss from the spot after a foul by Barcelona midfielder Rodri , before Spain mounted a comeback with Álex Baena pouncing on a poor possession loss from Nico O'Reilly, and Mikel Oyarzabal then giving Spain a 3-2 lead.

Fellow Real Madrid defender Dean Huijsen was also back in the squad after being left out of the World Cup, but was an unused substitute at Wembley on Saturday night.

articles.title: Has Ben White missed a huge opportunity with England? – Opinion
articles.summary: When Cole Palmer withdrew from international duty this week, Thomas Tuchel called it “another missed opportunity,” citing that the midfielder “misses way too...
articles.body:
When Cole Palmer withdrew from international duty this week, Thomas Tuchel called it "another missed opportunity," citing that the midfielder "misses way too many camps with injuries." as quoted by SkySports .

Unless he has an issue with the player's character, if the German is being consistent, then surely the same rationale applies to Ben White , also not in the current Three Lions squad due to injury?

Four different English players ended up at right-back in the last World Cup, so it's fair to say a fit-again White would have a great chance of playing in North America this summer.

After all, this is a defender who was starting in last season's run-in for the Champions and who, for years, has had a great partnership with Saka in front of him.

Yet increasingly, both his club and national managers are not having enough time to take advantage of that partnership.

Ben White's injuries continue to cost him opportunities

The 28-year-old missed the Champions League Final due to a serious knee issue.

A current groin problem is only a short-term issue and, from Arsenal 's point of view, the current break for the UEFA Nations fixtures gives the Gunner three weeks to rest.

Yet in terms of ambitions for his country, missing their next four games could be a huge blow.

On the pitch, White has nothing left to prove.

For a while, his only question mark has been: can his body handle a match every few days?

Four games in the next 11 days for England would have put him in pole position, but now someone else gets to run with the baton.

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Is White running out of time with England?

Many English fans won't sympathise and will even see the irony that White can't stay fit.

He's never publicly revealed why he made himself unavailable for selection during the Southgate era after coming home early from Qatar 2022.

Rumours have ranged from a falling out with Steve Holland to a struggle socially to mix with his peers.

Whatever the problem, it hasn't stopped the current regime from wanting him involved.

The mind is willing, but the body is not.

This might be the month Tuchel accepts that.

articles.title: FSU linebacker Chris Jones helped off field injured
articles.summary: Florida State linebacker Chris Jones was helped off the field with an apparent leg injury against Central Arkansas.
articles.body:
He was aided by members of the Seminoles' coaching staff and athletic trainers. He wasn't putting any weight on his left leg as he was helped off the field.

Jones had three total tackles in the game before he was helped off the field and brought into the medical tent.

The Seminoles currently lead Central Arkansas 24-7 in the third quarter at Doak Campbell Stadium.

Liam Rooney covers Florida State athletics for the Tallahassee Democrat. Contact him via email at LRooney@gannett.com or on Twitter @__liamrooney .

articles.title: ‘Sometime I lose focus’ – Lamine Yamal speaks out after Spain beat England
articles.summary: The Barcelona star opened the scoring at Wembley Stadium.
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal was on target for Spain during Saturday's 3-2 win over England and spoke to the media after the match about the victory.

The Barcelona teenager spoke about his opening goal and says Luis de la Fuente urges him to press high to try and win the ball up the pitch.

"That's what we try to do (always win). There's always someone who loses, but we try not to be the ones who lose. We know Wembley is very difficult," he told Teledeporte. "The manager really pushes us to press high, to believe we're going to win the ball, and that's what I've done. I always try to help the team. Sometimes I lose focus, but sometimes I steal the ball and find myself one-on-one and I'm able to score. "It doesn't bother us if the other team has the ball because we are very fast players and we know how to play on the counter-attack. You have to know what your role is in each match and we know how to do that."

articles.title: Leeds United Could Cash In On This Duo In January Window: Should They Sell Both?
articles.summary: Leeds United have reached the September international break sitting fifth in the Premier League, yet January planning has already begun at Elland Road. Accor...
articles.body:
Leeds United have reached the September international break sitting fifth in the Premier League, yet January planning has already begun at Elland Road. According to The Leeds Press , Lukas Nmecha and Dan James could both attract attention during the winter window.

Transfermarkt reportedly values the pair at £17.2 million combined. Nmecha joined Leeds United as a free agent last year and supplied useful depth behind Dominic Calvert-Lewin . The German finished the previous campaign as Leeds' third-highest scorer, but his contract now approaches its final months.

The Leeds Press report suggests the club have shown little urgency about extending Nmecha's deal. That situation could encourage Leeds to consider a January sale rather than risk losing the forward without a fee.

James faces a different situation. The Welsh winger produced 21 goal involvements during Leeds' Championship campaign, but injuries restricted him badly after promotion. Last season, the attacker failed to score or assist in the Premier League.

Fresh information indicates James won't push for a transfer, while Leeds would prefer to keep their squad together. Still, limited minutes under Daniel Farke have created uncertainty around his longer-term position.

Should Leeds United sell Lukas Nmecha and keep Dan James?

NOTTINGHAM, ENGLAND – AUGUST 25: Daniel James of Leeds United celebrates scoring his team's second goal with teammate Lukas Nmecha during the Carabao Cup Second Round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United at City Ground on August 25, 2026 in Nottingham, England. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images

Yes, the two cases should be treated very differently. Leeds should resist any January move for James because his pace, defensive work and top-flight experience give Farke another useful option from the bench. With the club sitting fifth, reducing the manager's wide choices midway through the season could create an avoidable problem.

James hasn't produced enough attacking numbers recently, but his value doesn't depend entirely on goals and assists. His ability to attack tired full-backs late in matches can change the shape of a game. He can press, track runners and stretch a defence when Leeds need fresh legs.

Nmecha presents a more straightforward decision. The striker is approaching the end of his contract, while Calvert-Lewin remains the established first-choice option. If Leeds don't plan to renew the German's deal, January could provide the last realistic chance to collect a meaningful fee.

An £8.6 million sale would represent pure transfer income after Nmecha arrived as a free agent. Leeds could then redirect that money towards a younger attacking option. Tom Cannon offers a physical domestic option, while Troy Parrott could provide link play and aerial threat from LaLiga. Jay Stansfield would bring energy and pressing intensity from Birmingham City .

Leeds' reported financial position gives the boardroom room to consider such a move. The summer departures reduced the wage burden, while previous sales generated accounting gains. A reported £22-25 million PSR cushion would further support January recruitment, although the club's exact internal position isn't public.

For Farke, keeping James preserves useful attacking depth. Selling Nmecha could create both financial room and a squad place, with Leeds United then able to seek another forward.

articles.title: Barcelona star leads Bruno Fernandes as Europe’s best long-term creator
articles.summary: Barcelona star Lamine Yamal has been the most prolific chance creator in European football’s leading leagues over the last three years. As much has this week...
articles.body:
Barcelona star Lamine Yamal has been the most prolific chance creator in European football's leading leagues over the last three years. As much has this week been confirmed by the statistics.

Winger Lamine has of course long established himself as the standout young talent across the globe. From his berth on Barcelona's right flank, the Spanish international has spent several years now terrorising opposing backlines with an elite combination of touch, dribbling, vision, passing and goalscoring.

Lamine's best quality is still up for debate, with the 19-year-old, despite his tender years, having already mastered so many different aspects of the game.

And one such ability, as alluded to above, has this week given rise to an altogether noteworthy statistic. The info comes courtesy of Squawka, who have revealed that Lamine has created more big chances than any other player in Europe's top-5 leagues since 2023/24.

The Barcelona prodigy leads the way with a total of 76, ahead of Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes in 2nd.
